description_en: Buṅga Bahī, also known as Prathampura Mahāvihāra, is located at the northwestern end of Buṅgamatī. The monument can be reached from the northern gate of the Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001). Thisbahīis in Lalitpur but is not counted among the majorbahīsof the district. It is named after Buṅgamatī, but is also referred to as Prathamapura Mahāvihāra, meaning the firstbahīof the area. It is under the ownership of local Śākyas. These people write their last name as Brahmācārya Bhikṣu.Thebahīhas four entrances, one at each of its four sides, but the eastern one forms the main entrance. Thebahī'ship roof is supported by plain struts, whilst the first floor is held up by double-layered pillars. As is often the case withbahī,one can find aphucāatop its roof. However, theśivaliṅga-shaped finial sets thisbahīapart from others; these structures generally have acaitya-shaped finial. A veranda surrounds the first floor of thebahīcomplex. Inside, an L-shaped staircase leads up to the first floor.The sanctum of thebahīis on the first floor of the western building and houses an east-facing statue of Akṣobhya. Two stone lions and two metal flags flank the entrance of the sanctum. Carved panels depicting a Gandharva, a female figure and a water vessel have been fixed on either side of the entrance.  Aśivaliṅga-shapedaśoka caityastands in the courtyard.No historical record could be found with which to date thebahī. However, a local folk tale tells that Matsyendranātha was brought to the Valley and requested to live in Bungmati. However, he replied that he did not want to dwell in a place without abahī. As a result, thisbahīwas constructed and the deity accepted the request to live here. According to thebahīmembers, thisbahīwas established by Dhyānacandra Miśra. Three merchant brothers from Patan, Dharmaśrī Miśra, Jñānaśrī Miśra and Dhyānacandra Miśra, spent the money they had earned through Tibetean trade to establish threebahīs. These are known as Kvanti Bahī, I Bahī and the presentbahī.However, no historical record is available to verify this claim. The only inscriptions found in thebahīcomplexstem from the late Malla period.Thebahīsuffered from multiple earthquakes and has undergone reconstruction multiple times. This took place most recently in 2005 and was carried out by the Department of Archeology in Nepal.The main worship rituals that take place are the annual ritual worship of thecaitya, a Vasundharā worship, a Mahākāla worship, and asrāddha(a ritual performed in honour of dead relatives) for Dhyānacandra Miśra. Aguṭhīendowed with 45ropanīof land in Bungmati and Sunaguthi was established to run the social and religious activities of thebahī(Locke 1985, 223). However, some of theguṭhī'slands have been privatised, and even the tenant farmers working the other lands no longer give thebahī'sshare to theguṭhī. Thesaṅgha-members of thebahītherefore rely on the collection of donations in order to fund these activities.
description_ne: ललितपुर जिल्लाभित्रै पर्ने भए पनि ललितपुरका प्रमुख बहीहरूको सूचीमा बुंग बहीलाई राखिएको छैन । बुंग (बुंगमती) क्षेत्रको बही हुनाले यसलाई बुंग बही भनिएको हो । बुंगमती क्षेत्रमा स्थापना भएको पहिलो विहार हुनाले यसलाई संस्कृतमा प्रथमपुर महाविहार नामाकरण गरिएको भन्ने भनाइ छ । यो शाक्यहरूको बही हो । यहाँका शाक्यहरू आफ्नो थर 'ब्रम्हचर्य भिक्षु' लेख्छन् । अन्य बहीमा जस्तै यो बहीमा पनि छानामाथि पुल (फुचा) बनाइएको छ, तर पुलमाथि कलशाकार वा चैत्याकार गजूर नराखी शिवलिंग आकारको गजूर राखिएको छ । बहीको पहिलो तलामा चारैतिर बरण्डा निकालिएको छ । बहीको भुइँतलामा गन्धकुटी रहेको छ जसभित्र पूर्वाभिमुख गरी अक्षोभ्यको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । गन्धकुटीमा जाने सिँढीको दायाँ-बायाँ एक जोडी सिंह र धातुको झण्डा राखिएको छ । बही प्राङ्गणमा शिवलिङ्ग स्वरूपको अशोक चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ ।यो बही कसले कुन समयमा निर्माण गरे भन्ने सम्बन्धमा तथ्य प्रमाणहरूको अभाव रहेको छ । स्थानीय वासिन्दाहरूका अनुसार रातो मच्छिन्द्रनाथलाई नेपालमा ल्याएपछि बुंगमतीमा राख्न खोज्दा "विहार नभएको ठाउँमा म वास गर्दिन" भनेकोले यो विहार बनाइएको थियो र यो विहार बनिसकेपछि मात्र मच्छिन्द्रनाथलाई बुंगमतीमा विराजमान गराइएको थियो । बहीका संघ-सदस्यहरूका अनुसार यो बही ध्यानचन्द्र मिश्रले स्थापना गरेका थिए । पाटनका तीनजना दाजुभाइहरू धर्मश्री मिश्र, ज्ञानश्री मिश्र र ध्यानचन्द्र मिश्रले तिब्बतमा व्यापार गरी कमाएको सम्पत्तिले क्रमशः क्वन्ति बही, ईबही र बुंग बही निर्माण गरेका थिए । तर यस कुरालाई प्रमाणित गर्ने कुनै ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण पाइएको छैन । यहाँ उत्तर-मध्यकालदेखिका मात्र अभिलेख पाइएका छन् । पटक-पटकको भूकम्पले क्षति पुगेको यो बहीको धेरैपल्ट जीर्णोद्धार भइसकेको छ । यहाँ नित्यपूजा लगायत चैत्यको वर्षवर्द्धन, वसुन्धरा पूजा, महाकाल पूजा, औंसी पूजा, बहीका संस्थापक ध्यानचन्द्र मिश्रको श्राद्ध लगायतका पर्व-गुठीहरू संचालनमा छन् । बही चलाउन आयस्रोतको रूपमा ४५ रोपनी जग्गा गुठी राखिएको थियो (Locke 1985, 223) । बुंगमती र सुनागुथिमा रहेका ती जग्गामध्ये केही व्यक्तिगत नाममा दर्ता भइसकेका छन् भने केही खेतबाट बाली उठाउन सकिएको छैन । त्यसैले बहीका संघ-सदस्यहरूबाट नै चन्दा उठाई बहीको पूजा संचालन भइरहेको छ ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: The Bahī complex collapsed in the 1833 (NS 953) earthquake. After the earthquake, the Bahī was reconstructed reestablishing the statues of Vajravārāhī, Prajñāpāramitā and Sarasvatī.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of a container, mohara and toraṇa
historical_events.event_description: Brahmācārya Bhikṣus of the Bahī, namely Rāja Vidhi, Lakṣmī Vidhi and other 16 people offered a round-shaped pot (bidola) to Akṣobhya and 10 garlands of coins (mohara mālā) to Matsyendranātha.Images of four donors are sculpted at the bottom of the inscription.
The Bahī complex collapsed in the 1934 earthquake. Theguṭhī-members of the Bahī reconstructed it.
Department of Archaeology, Nepal renovated the Bahī complex.
Due to the 2015 earthquake, some of the parts of the Bahī are damaged.
Dharmasena, Lakudeva and others repaired the Bahī.
Statues of Kranajoti (Karṇajyoti) and his wife were established towards south from the sanctum’s entrance.
Buddhirāja, with the help of his grandson, made adharmadhātujinālaya caityain front of the southern door of the Bahī.
Gaṇeśamān Śākya made adharmadhātujinālaya caityain front of the southern door of the Bahī.

historical_events.event_name: Copying the regulation of the Bahī
historical_events.event_description: The regulations of the Bahī according to this inscription, which in earlier times was written in the leaves of a Peepal tree, were copied in the present stone inscription, which regulates to collect money for its reconstruction from the harvest of itsguṭhī-lands located in Nakkhu and Gakhapā. All thebahī-members should participate in the task, otherwise, their sin would be counted as five grave sins or offences (pañcamahāpātaka).  This inscription, placed at the northern corner of the sanctum records three historical events and three different era years.
The inscription mentions that apānejuof the Buṅgmatī temple performed some acts in the Buṅga Bahī. However, the act could not be figured out due to the condition of the inscription.
